paragraphs.title: The People's Distress and Debt Bondage

easy.explanation: Their cry was against their fellow Jews.
easy.q: Against whom did the people and their wives cry?

easy.explanation: They needed corn so they might eat and live.
easy.q: What did some people say they needed to obtain so they might eat and live?

easy.explanation: Some families brought their sons and daughters into bondage.
easy.q: What did some families bring into bondage to be servants?

answers: To buy corn because of the dearth
To buy tools for the wall
medium.explanation: They mortgaged their property to buy corn because of the famine.
medium.q: Why had some people mortgaged their lands, vineyards, and houses?

medium.explanation: They borrowed money to pay the king's tribute.
medium.q: Why had some people borrowed money?

answers: They could not free them from bondage
They could not find them houses
medium.explanation: They lacked the ability to redeem their daughters from servitude.
medium.q: What did the people mean by saying it was not in their power to redeem their daughters?

answers: Dearth, borrowing, mortgaging property, and bondage
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from lack of corn to debt, loss of property, and bondage.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the people's distress?

answers: The Jews were one people, making the oppression of brethren especially wrong
The people wanted food from the heathen
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the common identity and brotherhood of the Jews.
challenge.q: What does the statement, “our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren,” emphasize?

answers: They could not work on the wall
Other men had their lands and vineyards
They could not travel to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Their lands and vineyards had passed into the hands of others.
challenge.q: Which complaint shows that the families had lost economic independence?

easy.q: How did Nehemiah react when he heard the people's cry?

easy.explanation: He rebuked the nobles and the rulers.

answers: Exacting money and corn as usury
easy.explanation: He asked them to leave off exacting money and corn as usury.
easy.q: What did Nehemiah ask himself, his brethren, and his servants to stop doing?

answers: To recall that Jews had been redeemed from bondage
To request more money from the heathen
To explain how to build the wall
medium.explanation: He recalled their redemption to emphasize the duty to treat Jewish brethren rightly.
medium.q: Why did Nehemiah mention Jews who had been sold unto the heathen?

medium.explanation: The nobles were leaders or people of high rank whom Nehemiah confronted.
medium.q: In this passage, who were the nobles?

answers: They should walk in the fear of God
medium.explanation: Nehemiah asked whether they ought to walk in the fear of God.
medium.q: What moral reason did Nehemiah give for changing their behavior?

answers: Their conduct could bring shame upon Israel before its enemies
The heathen helped build the wall
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah warned that their conduct would bring reproach before the heathen.
challenge.q: Why did Nehemiah mention the reproach of the heathen?

answers: They also had the ability to exact money and corn, but were willing to stop
They owed money to the poor
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah said that he, his brethren, and his servants could exact money and corn, but asked them to stop.
challenge.q: Why did Nehemiah include himself and his men in his appeal?

answers: They held their peace and found nothing to answer
challenge.explanation: The nobles and rulers were silent and had no answer.
challenge.q: How did the nobles and rulers respond after Nehemiah challenged them?

paragraphs.title: Restoring Property and Swearing to Keep the Decision

answers: Their lands, vineyards, oliveyards, houses, and money
easy.explanation: Nehemiah commanded them to restore the property and money taken from the poor.
easy.q: What did Nehemiah command the leaders to restore?

easy.explanation: Nehemiah called the priests and took an oath of them.
easy.q: Whom did Nehemiah call to witness the promise?

easy.explanation: All the congregation said, “Amen,” and praised the LORD.
easy.q: What did all the congregation say after Nehemiah shook his lap?

answers: The money, corn, wine, and oil they had exacted
medium.explanation: They were to restore the property and give up the money and produce they had exacted.
medium.q: What did the lenders have to give up besides the property?

answers: It made their agreement a binding promise
It allowed them to take more property
medium.explanation: The oath formally bound them to carry out their promise.
medium.q: Why was the oath important after the people said, “We will restore them”?

answers: That those who broke the promise would be emptied out
medium.explanation: It symbolized God's judgment on anyone who failed to keep the promise.
medium.q: What did Nehemiah's shaking out of his lap symbolize?

answers: The poor would receive back the resources taken from them
The nobles would receive more land
The people would stop working on the wall
challenge.explanation: Restoration returned the economic resources that had been taken from the poor.
challenge.q: How would restoring the property correct the injustice?

answers: The restoration was to happen immediately
The restoration would wait until the next year
The restoration would happen only during a feast
challenge.explanation: The phrase stresses that the property should be restored at once.
challenge.q: What does “even this day” emphasize in Nehemiah's command?

answers: A demand for restoration, agreement, an oath, and a symbolic warning
A feast, a war, a new tax, and construction
A sale, a loan, an escape, and a return
challenge.explanation: That is the order of events in these verses.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the events?

easy.explanation: He served from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year, twelve years.
easy.q: How long did Nehemiah serve as governor?

easy.explanation: He said, “I and my brethren have not eaten the bread of the governor.”
easy.q: What did Nehemiah not eat during his governorship?

easy.explanation: His servants were gathered to the work of the wall.

answers: They were chargeable unto the people and took provisions from them
They gave the people their own fields
medium.explanation: The former governors burdened the people and took bread, wine, and money.
medium.q: How had the former governors treated the people?

answers: They remained focused on the work of the wall
The people forbade them to work
medium.explanation: Their attention was devoted to the work of the wall.
medium.q: Why did Nehemiah and his servants not buy land?

answers: They placed a heavy financial burden on the people
They made life easier for the people
They led the people into battle
medium.explanation: The phrase means that they imposed a burden on the people.
medium.q: What does “chargeable unto the people” mean?

answers: Because of the fear of God
Because he wanted to buy fields
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah said he did not act that way because of the fear of God.
challenge.q: Why did Nehemiah refuse to act like the former governors?

answers: Former governors burdened the people, but Nehemiah did not
Former governors built the wall, but Nehemiah destroyed it
Nehemiah bought fields, but the former governors gave them away
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah contrasts his conduct with that of the governors before him.
challenge.q: What contrast is central in these verses?

answers: He kept his servants focused on the public work instead of private gain
He used the wall to collect taxes
He abandoned the people during construction
challenge.explanation: His servants were gathered to the work, showing his commitment to the public project.
challenge.q: How does Nehemiah's work on the wall reveal his leadership priorities?

paragraphs.title: Nehemiah's Table and His Prayer for Remembrance

answers: Jews, rulers, and people who came from the surrounding heathen
easy.explanation: One hundred fifty Jews and rulers ate at his table, along with visitors from the surrounding area.

answers: An ox, six choice sheep, fowls, and wine
easy.explanation: The passage lists an ox, six choice sheep, fowls, and wine.
easy.q: What food was prepared for Nehemiah's table?

easy.explanation: Nehemiah prayed, “Think upon me, my God, for good.”
easy.q: What did Nehemiah ask God to do at the end of the chapter?

answers: He planned to sell the food
medium.explanation: A large number of Jews, rulers, and visitors ate at his table.
medium.q: Why was much food prepared at Nehemiah's table?

medium.explanation: He did not require the governor's provisions.
medium.q: What did Nehemiah still not require despite the expense of the table?

answers: The work and burden upon the people were severe
The people had finished all their work
medium.explanation: Nehemiah recognized that the people were under a heavy burden.
medium.q: What does “the bondage was heavy upon this people” mean?

answers: He bore the expense of hospitality rather than add to the people's burden
He provided food for no one
He made the poor pay for every meal
challenge.explanation: He fed many people but did not claim the governor's provisions because the people were heavily burdened.
challenge.q: What does Nehemiah's table, together with his refusal of the governor's bread, show?

answers: It shows hospitality and responsibility toward leaders, workers, and visitors
It shows that he withdrew from the people
It was used to collect debts
challenge.explanation: His table served a broad community connected with the work and public life.
challenge.q: How does the table relate to Nehemiah's leadership?

answers: Because the bondage was heavy upon the people
challenge.explanation: He refused the governor's provisions because the people were already carrying a heavy burden.
challenge.q: Why did Nehemiah not require the bread of the governor?
